title: File:Chery Tiggo 7 Sport front.jpg
author: Rutger van der Maar
description:
Place: Guangzhou, Guangdong Province
Chinese name:  奇瑞瑞虎7 (qíruì ruìhǔ 7)
Year of launch: 2016
Chery Automobile was the largest Chinese carmaker for quite some time, thanks to successes of the QQ, Tiggo, A5 and the old Windcloud/Flagcloud (Fulwin/Cowin) models. Chery is a state-owned company founded in 1997. It began automobile production in 1999 after acquiring toolings and a license to produce the first generation Seat Toledo. Interesting is that Chery was only granted a production license for passenger cars in 2003, which means Chery cars couldn't be legally sold until 2001. Until then Chery was officially only producing automotive components, albeit in a fully assembled form. In 2001 Chery solved the problem by piggybacking on a SAIC Motor license, China's largest state-owned car manufacturer. Chery surely knowns the way around the law... After rising tensions between Chery Automobile and General Motors (GM) and Volkswagen, two of SAIC's joint venture partners, the 20% ownership SAIC once held in Chery was sold. GM was not amused and filed lawsuits after Chery copied their Spark (Matiz) and Epica (Evanda/Magnus) models. Volkswagen also planned a lawsuit against Chery, because they apparently secretly purchased the Seat Toledo blueprints, which is quite interesting considering Seat is a subsidiary of Volkswagen...

Thanks to the newly launched models, the successful Arrizo 5 sedan, Chery Tiggo 7 and the recently launched second generation Tiggo 5, Chery seems to have found new success. The Tiggo 7 is competing with the Changan CS75, Geely Boyue, Haval H6 and Trumpchi GS4. It was the production version of the Chery TX Concept, which was showcased in 2012. I think it is currently one of the best looking Chinese cars on the market.

title: File:Chevrolet Spark (US) (7452907692).jpg
author: InSapphoWeTrust from Los Angeles, California, USA
description:
The Spark is Chevrolet's newest and smallest car, going on sale in the US market in summer 2012 as a 2013 model. It is the newest iteration of the model that many countries have been getting as the Daewoo Matiz and the Chevrolet Matiz; Daewoo had produced its first Matiz back in 1999, and Daewoo's 2002 bankruptcy and subsequent acquisition by General Motors brought the Matiz into the General Motors portfolio.
A nicely appointed interior with leather seats and an armrest, even though this is a very small lightweight city car, and feels the part with the rather cheap feel as the doors close. On a bare-bones car like this, I'd lose most of the upscale options, and even drop the automatic to make full use of the engine's limited power.

Seen at Barrett-Jackson Auction.

title: File:Chevrolet Spark, Sonic, Cruze (US) (7452907478).jpg
author: InSapphoWeTrust from Los Angeles, California, USA
description:
Chevrolet's economy car lineup, which used to consist of miserable rental fleet fodder like the Cavalier/Cobalt and the Aveo, now looks a lot better, with GM finally dipping into its overseas resources to produce competitive models for worldwide sales.

All three of these cars are from GM Korea, which used to be known as Daewoo. The right, the Cruze, has replaced both the Cavalier/Cobalt and the Daewoo Lacetti (Suzuki Forenza/Chevrolet Optra), and with fuel-efficient Opel powertrain, has been fairly well received. The middle, the Sonic, replaces the Aveo and is a far better car. The left, the Spark, is the newest member of the trio, and it is the newest iteration of the car that used to be marketed in many overseas markets as the Daewoo Matiz or the Chevrolet Matiz.

For the US market, the Cruze is built in Lordstown, Ohio, at the same plant that used to build the Cavalier/Cobalt. The Sonic's production has also moved stateside, taking place at Orion Township, Michigan. The Spark is produced by GM Korea, at the same Incheon assembly plant that used to crank out the Aveo, the Lacetti/Forenza/Optra, and the Daewoo-branded vehicles.

Seen at Barrett-Jackson Auction.
